source:
SUPER-PROMPT: "STREET STRIKERS" - Arcade Soccer (one-shot build)
Build a complete, polished, mobile-first arcade soccer game called Street Strikers. Fast, punchy, easy to learn in 5 seconds, hard to put down. Rocket-League-meets-street-football energy: power shots, air control, big satisfying goals. It must be fully playable solo - empty server slots are filled by AI bots that seamlessly hand off to real players as they join. Prioritize game feel, low latency, and retention above visual realism.
1. Core game loop

3v3 matches on a compact enclosed street pitch (walls, no out-of-bounds - ball ricochets, keeps play continuous and fast). Rounds are 3 minutes. First to loop back after golden-goal if tied.
Flow: Lobby → Matchmaking countdown (10s, backfilled instantly with bots) → Kickoff → Match → Goal celebration + slow-mo replay → Post-match rewards screen → back to lobby.
Never make a player wait for humans. A match ALWAYS starts on time; open slots are bots. When a human joins mid-queue or mid-match, they take over the weakest bot on the team that needs balancing, at that bot's position, with a 1s "SUBBED IN" banner.

2. Controls (mobile-first, one-thumb friendly)

Left: floating thumbstick for movement. Right: a single context-action button that changes based on state - when you don't have the ball it's Tackle/Slide; when you have it, tap = Pass, hold = Charge Shot (power meter fills, release to fire). Second small button = Sprint/Dash (short cooldown burst).
Auto-detect input: show touch UI on mobile, keybinds on PC (WASD, Space=shoot/hold-to-charge, Shift=sprint, E=pass/tackle, gamepad supported).
Aim assist: shots and passes gently snap toward the goal/nearest teammate based on facing - tunable, generous on mobile.

3. Ball physics & networking (CRITICAL - get this right)
The ball is the whole game; latency here ruins everything. Implement these exactly:

The ball is a single spherical BasePart with tuned CustomPhysicalProperties (moderate density ~1.2, elasticity ~0.5 for lively bounces, low friction, friction/elasticity weights set so wall ricochets feel snappy). Real Roblox physics - never Tween or CFrame-lerp the ball's gameplay position.
Dynamic network ownership: by default the server owns the ball (ball:SetNetworkOwner(nil)). The instant a player is the last to touch it / is the closest controller, hand ownership to that player's client via SetNetworkOwner(player) so their dribbling is zero-latency and buttery on their screen. Hand ownership back to the server the moment the ball leaves their control radius, goes airborne from a shot, or after a short timeout. Debounce ownership changes (min ~0.25s hold) to avoid thrashing.
Server authority + anti-exploit: server validates every ball interaction. Clamp max ball speed, validate that a "kick" came from a player actually near the ball, and sanity-check position deltas. Never trust client-reported ball position for goals - the server confirms goals from its own physics state.
Client-side prediction & interpolation: non-owning clients interpolate the ball smoothly between replicated states (short buffer, ~100ms, lerp) so it never teleports/jitters under packet loss. The owning client sees instant response.
Use RemoteEvents (unreliable remotes for high-frequency cosmetic ball spin/particles, reliable remotes for kicks/goals). Keep replication payloads tiny.
Kicks apply an impulse (ApplyImpulse/AssemblyLinearVelocity) computed on the server after validation, with the charge meter mapping to force and an upward arc component for lobs/volleys.

4. Player movement & characters

Snappy custom-tuned Humanoid: higher WalkSpeed than default, quick acceleration, responsive turning. Add a short dash (impulse + brief cooldown + trail effect).
Ball control: a soft "dribble radius" - while you have possession the ball is nudged ahead of you via physics forces (not welded), so tackles can steal it and it feels physical.
Skill move: double-tap dash = a quick juke/feint with a small hitbox dodge and stylish animation.
Goalkeeper role auto-assigned to whichever teammate is deepest, or a dedicated bot keeper with dive animations.

5. AI players (must feel alive, not robotic)
Do NOT rely on raw PathfindingService for chasing - it's too slow/rigid for soccer. Build a lightweight behavior-tree / finite-state-machine steering AI run on the server on Heartbeat:

States: Chase, Dribble, Pass, Shoot, Support (make space / run to open lane), Defend/Mark, Intercept, Return-to-formation, Goalkeep. Use steering behaviors (seek, arrive, pursue the ball's predicted position, separation from teammates, flee-to-defend).
Bots understand roles and formation - they don't all swarm the ball. One presses, others hold shape and offer passing lanes. They pass to open teammates, shoot when in range with a clear angle, and defend when the enemy has the ball.
Difficulty scales with lobby: reaction time, pass accuracy, shot power/accuracy, and anticipation all tuned by a single difficulty float (0-1). Give bots slight imperfection (occasional miss, slight reaction delay) so they feel human and beatable - perfect bots are unfun.
Bots have names, jersey numbers, and cosmetics like players so the roster looks real. Seamless takeover: a bot swapped for a human keeps position/momentum.
Use spatial queries / raycasts for "is a passing lane open," not expensive per-frame pathfinding. Throttle heavy AI decisions to ~5-10Hz, keep steering per-frame.

6. Game feel / "juice" (this is what makes it replayable)
Layer these aggressively - this is the single biggest driver of fun:

Hit-stop / freeze-frame for a few ms on powerful kicks and tackles.
Screen shake scaled to shot power and goals.
Ball trail and speed lines on power shots; a sonic-boom ring on max-charge strikes.
Charge-up: ball glows and pulses, controller rumbles (gamepad), power meter fills with color ramp (green→yellow→red).
Goal moment: freeze → zoom → slow-mo replay of the last ~3s from a dynamic camera → confetti/pyro particles → crowd roar SFX → big animated "GOAAAL!" text with the scorer's name → net ripple physics.
Sound is non-negotiable: distinct SFX for kick, pass, tackle, wall bounce (pitch-varied), whistle, crowd swells, UI clicks, announcer barks ("What a strike!"). Punchy music in lobby, tense stinger near golden goal.
Camera: slightly dynamic - subtle follow, pulls back a touch during fast play, cinematic angle on goals. Never disorienting.
Every UI interaction animates (buttons scale/bounce, rewards pop in with tweens + sound). No static screens.

7. Progression & retention systems

XP + Levels earned per match (goals, assists, tackles, wins). Level-up popup with reward.
Two currencies: soft (Coins, earned) and premium (Gems, Robux/optional). Coins buy cosmetics; Gems for premium/skip.
Cosmetics (core of the economy): jerseys, cleats, ball skins (with unique trails/SFX), goal-celebration emotes, nameplates, player trails. Purely cosmetic - never pay-to-win. Cosmetic ball skins that change the trail are huge for clip-ability.
Daily login rewards (escalating 7-day streak), daily/weekly quests ("score 5 goals," "win 3 matches"), and a free + premium Battle Pass / season track with fresh cosmetics each season.
Ranked ladder (Bronze→Elite) with a visible rank badge, MMR, and season resets - gives skilled players a reason to grind. Casual "Quick Play" always available and always bot-backed.
Stats profile: career goals, win rate, top plays. People love seeing their numbers climb.
"Play again" one-tap on the post-match screen to instantly requeue - minimize friction between matches.

8. Social / virality hooks

Post-goal auto-saved replay the player can rewatch/share - designed to be clippable for TikTok/YouTube Shorts (this is how Roblox games grow).
Emotes/celebrations, team chat, quick-chat wheel ("Nice!", "My bad", "Pass!").
Party/friends system to queue together and fill remaining slots with bots.
Referral or group-join reward, and a spot for a Roblox group with a join bonus.

9. Data & backend (best practices)

Persist player data (level, XP, currencies, owned cosmetics, equipped loadout, stats, rank, quest progress, battle-pass tier) with a robust session-locked DataStore pattern (ProfileService/ProfileStore-style) - session locking to prevent duplication/data loss, auto-retry, and safe autosave + BindToClose save on shutdown.
Never store gameplay currency client-side as source of truth; server authoritative for all economy transactions.
Validate all purchases server-side; process MarketplaceService receipts idempotently (ProcessReceipt with granted-tracking so double-grants can't happen).

10. Performance & architecture

Clean client-server split: server = authoritative simulation (ball, scoring, AI, economy); client = input, prediction, UI, and all cosmetic effects. Never run gameplay logic that matters on the client alone.
Modular, readable Luau: organize into services/modules (MatchService, BallController, AIController, EconomyService, UIController, DataService). Use ModuleScripts, a clear folder structure, and a lightweight event bus. Type-check where reasonable.
Optimize: pool particles/effects (don't spawn/destroy constantly), throttle non-critical loops, use RunService.Heartbeat for physics-tied logic and RenderStepped only for client visuals/camera, minimize per-frame allocations, and use CollectionService tags for entity management.
Mobile performance target: smooth on low-end phones - keep part counts and effects budgeted, LOD the crowd/environment, and cap particle density.
Streaming-friendly, small arena so everything stays loaded and responsive.

11. Onboarding (first 60 seconds decide retention)

New player drops straight into a match vs bots - no menus first. Learn by playing.
Contextual tooltips fade in for the first match only ("Hold to charge a shot!"). First goal triggers an extra-big celebration + a starter reward to hook them.
Give every new player a free starter cosmetic immediately so they feel ownership.

12. Art direction

Clean, colorful, slightly stylized street/urban pitches (rooftop, alley, neon night court, beach) - bright, readable, mobile-legible. High contrast so the ball is always visible. Multiple maps in rotation for variety.

Deliver a fully functional, well-organized, exploit-resistant, mobile-first game with all of the above. When in doubt, prioritize: responsive ball feel > game-feel juice > retention systems > visual fidelity.

answers.ask: How large should the pitch be - a tight 3v3 street court of roughly 150 studs, or something closer to a full-size pitch?
answers.answer: Use a tight 3v3 enclosed street court of roughly 150 studs; the compact scale is essential to the fast, continuous arcade pace.

answers.ask: Should the four pitch themes ship as one map redressed, or as four separate maps in a rotation?
answers.answer: Use one compact pitch layout redressed into the four themes, keeping collision and gameplay consistent while making the build smaller and polished.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D arcade soccer map centered on one compact, enclosed 3v3 street court roughly 150 studs across. The rectangular pitch is bounded on all sides by solid rebound walls, with goals centered at the two short ends and no out-of-bounds space; keep the court open, highly readable, and framed for fast continuous play. Build one consistent collision layout that can be redressed as four colorful, stylized urban-themed variants: a rooftop pitch, narrow alley court, neon night court, and beach court. Use high-contrast surfacing and clear sightlines so the ball and goals remain visible from a slightly elevated, dynamic gameplay camera.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Sports: the original specifies timed 3v3 soccer matches, goals, and a compact competitive field. There is no secondary genre.

### Shape and preset
Use `space-bounded`, a single rectangular street-football court whose solid perimeter keeps the ball in continuous play. Match the Physics Sport preset: its enclosed, rebound-friendly field model fits arcade soccer better than a regulation open pitch. Retain the preset’s visible goal-and-wall logic, but omit an elaborate stadium treatment.

### Config requirements
Use `barrier-perimeter` as solid rebound walls on all four sides, flush with the court boundary and high enough to keep the ball in play. Use `trigger-scoring` as two clearly legible goal mouths centered in the short-end walls, with contrasting nets and frames that remain visible from the elevated gameplay view.

### Layout requirements
Place `trigger-scoring` twice: one scoring volume immediately inside each of the two end goals, spanning the full goal mouth behind the line. The two volumes must be mirrored across the court’s long axis and sit entirely within the rebound-wall boundary.

### Layout components
Build one compact, open rectangular 3v3 court roughly 150 studs across, with a broad uninterrupted central play area and no out-of-bounds apron. Put two identical goals at the centers of the opposing short ends. Solid continuous rebound walls enclose all four sides and meet the goal structures cleanly, leaving no escape gaps or dead corners. Keep surfacing high-contrast and uncluttered, with clear long sightlines between both goals for a slightly elevated dynamic camera.

This is one authoritative collision layout, redressed rather than duplicated into four variants: a rooftop pitch with skyline edge dressing beyond the walls; a narrow alley court with urban facades outside the enclosure; a neon night court with luminous trim and dark surroundings; and a beach court with bright sand-adjacent scenery beyond the same walls. These are visual skins of the same court, not separate maps. Frame the isometric composition diagonally so both goals, the full perimeter, and the open center read at once.

### Render order
Use `isometric`: the topology is a simple, symmetric enclosed court, so the visual presentation can lead and the top-down plan can be projected from it.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale band: small, driven by the single roughly 150-stud 3v3 court. Theme: clean, colorful, stylized arcade street football with mobile-legible contrast. Pipeline modifier: `P0`; one flat, enclosed court is fully captured in a single top-down surface, and the four themes are redresses rather than separate spaces.
